content.rationale: The node-set module. It enumerates the node ids from jj — the candidate listing of the changes touching `nodes/`, each kept only where the change carries its own document `nodes/<its own change id>.json` (D1b), so a change that only touches the path is not a node (S2-set, ryzlzrkk) — through the runner (M-jj, zruxtxrv) rather than the working copy's directory; a candidate whose own document is absent is dropped as not-a-node, while every other load failure is read through the read interface (S2-read, nqktpzuu) and surfaced as a value rather than an abort; the caller — log's all-or-nothing read, validate's per-node report — decides what a failure means. It names ids through store_path (vkztyrzm) and loads through node_load (sxonuzmr); D3 (volxoyyy) fixes the edges to report and D4 (mqqwzvwz) that targets are sibling ids with the root excepted, while S2-path (pumpuqkv) fixes the one layout and S2-invalid (uzvzopwp) the failure shape. M-layout (szmuyqrq) places the module flat at src/node_set.rs, and I1-serde (orrvsxqq) fixes the JSON layer it is written against. The set no longer loads each document itself: it enumerates the candidate ids, hands them to M-store-bulk (xlvtxsky), and maps each returned document to Loaded, each absence to a skip, and each failure to Failed. The enumeration also reports the order jj listed the candidates, and the set keeps it: `list_ordered` yields each node — its id, its document and edges, or its failure, with the same skip of a candidate that owns no document — in the order jj listed it, so a verb that reports the set reports what jj said instead of an invented order; `list` is that same ordered set keyed by id, unchanged in signature and in its id ordering, so the callers that look a node up by id (log's read, validate's per-node report) are untouched. Reporting the set is now also reporting what it leaves out: `list_with_drops` returns `list_ordered`'s set, entry for entry and in the same order, together with the ids of exactly the candidates dropped for want of `nodes/<their own id>.json`, and nothing else — a candidate whose document is present but does not load stays a node carrying Failed, not a drop. The drops are reported as a set, and reporting one adds nothing to the node set: the nodes and the drops are disjoint and together account for exactly the candidates the enumeration listed, once each, so a change that merely touches `nodes/` is visible to the caller without ever being resolved as a node. All three entry points are views of one private read — it enumerates, batches through M-store-bulk, and maps the outcomes once — so `list_ordered` and `list` keep behaving exactly as they did, signature and semantics unchanged, and the drop report is a second view of the same read rather than a second enumeration.
